ERNMEN€ ECORCS CONTROL NO. ATTY. FERDINAND L. PANES, CESE City Director DILG-110ilo City Office 3F, Angeles Arcade Mabini Street, Iloilo City Dear Atty. Panes: DILG Legal Opinion No. 88 s. NOV 28 2011, This has reference to your 13 October 2011 letter requesting the Department's opinion on whether the Sangguniang Barangay has the authority to declare the barangay under a state of calamity under RA 10121 for purposes of utilizing the 30% of the 5% LDRRMF allocated as quick response fund (QRF). Sec. 16 of RA 10121 and Rule 12 of its IRR provides that the declaration and lifting of the state of calamity may be declared by the President upon recommendation of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC). This may also be issued by the local sanggunian upon the recommendation of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (LDRRMC), based on the results of the damage assessment and needs analysis. The LDRRMCs in barangays are now named as Barangay Development Councils (BDCs). It assumed the powers and functions of the dissolved Barangay Disaster Coordinating Councils. On the other hand, the provision on the utilization of the LDRRMF is found under Sec. 21 of RA 10121 and Rule 18 of its IRR. Pursuant thereto, Local Government Units are mandated to set aside not less than 5% of the estimated revenue from regular sources as the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) to support disaster risk management activities. Based on the foregoing, the Sangguniang Barangay may declare a barangay under a state of calamity upon recommendation of the BDC for purposes of utilizing the 30% of the 5% LDRRMF allocated as quick response fund. It must be noted however that LDRRMF releases as well as its utilization, accounting and auditing shall be subject to the NDRRMC's guidelines and procedures. We hope the foregoing sufficiently addresses your concern. Very truly yours, J US B. Director I LS08:rb
